notes: Recommends MORE structure up front (csv/, jobs/, status/ subfolders, multiple files each) — the opposite of the skill's 'start coarser' thesis. This is the eval where the skill changes the answer most.

Baseline (no skill) is already strong at 75% — modern Claude reasons well about AI-aware code organisation unaided. The skill's job is consistency and the specific framing, not reversing wrong answers.
Eval 0 (split-growing-component): both configs pass 4/4. The skill adds nothing on net here — the base model already pushes back on the 3-way split and recommends hooks.

Eval 2 (structure-new-module) is where the skill earns its keep: the baseline recommends MORE structure up front (csv/jobs/status subfolders), directly contradicting the 'start coarser' thesis. With the skill it reliably advises starting coarse and splitting at ~300 lines.
The skill costs ~+2.6k tokens and ~+1s — negligible. No time/quality tradeoff worth worrying about.
Single run per configuration — without_skill pass-rate stddev reflects across-eval variance, not run-to-run flakiness. Consider 3 runs/config before drawing strong conclusions.
